@settingsBack.description: Tooltip of the back button on the Settings screen

@settingsSaveLocation.description: Settings row: where received files are saved

@settingsSaveLocationPath.description: Settings row caption: the folder received files go to (Downloads folder, then Linksy subfolder)

@settingsAcceptFromMyDevices.description: Settings switch: accept files from paired devices automatically

settingsAcceptFromMyDevicesCaption: Files from paired devices arrive without asking.

@settingsStayConnected.description: Settings switch: keep connections to nearby devices open

settingsStayConnectedCaption: Faster sharing with nearby devices. Uses more battery.

@settingsStayConnectedCaption.description: Caption of the Stay connected switch

@settingsKeepRunning.description: Settings switch: keep the app running when closed

settingsKeepRunningCaption: Files, photo backup and calls keep working when Linksy is closed. Shows a quiet notification.

@settingsAwayFromHome.description: Settings switch: reach computers over the internet

settingsAwayFromHomeCaption: Reach your computers over the internet when you’re not on the same network, for a week after you last were. Encrypted end to end.

@settingsAwayFromHomeCaption.description: Caption of the Away from home switch

@settingsWithYourComputers.description: Settings section label: features shared with paired computers

@settingsPauseMusic.description: Settings switch: computers pause media during phone calls

settingsPauseMusicCaption: Your computers pause what plays while a call rings or goes on, and resume after.

@settingsPauseMusicCaption.description: Caption of the Pause music switch

@settingsBrowseFiles.description: Settings switch: share a phone folder with computers

settingsBrowseFilesChoose: Choose a folder your computers can open in their Files app, like Documents (Android doesn’t allow Download).

@settingsBrowseFilesChoose.description: Caption when no shared folder is chosen yet

settingsSharesFolder: Shares “{folder}”. Tap to choose another folder.

@settingsSharesFolder.description: Caption showing the folder shared with computers

@settingsPicture.description: Settings row: the picture computers show for this phone

settingsPictureChoose: Your computers show it for this phone. Tap to choose one.

@settingsPictureChoose.description: Caption when no picture is chosen

settingsPictureChange: Your computers show it for this phone. Tap to change it.

@settingsPictureChange.description: Caption when a picture is chosen

@settingsPictureRemove.description: Button that removes the phone picture

@settingsLocate.description: Settings switch: allow computers to ask for the phone location

settingsLocateCaption: A computer can ask where this phone is, once, to find it. Nothing is kept or tracked. Works while Linksy is open.
settingsLocatePermission: Linksy needs the location permission for this.

@settingsLocatePermission.description: Message when the location permission was refused

@settingsPhotoFolder.description: Settings row: the camera folder backed up to computers

settingsPhotoFolderChoose: Choose your camera folder (DCIM › Camera) to back up photos to a computer.

@settingsPhotoFolderChoose.description: Caption when no photo folder is chosen

settingsPhotoFolderBacksUp: Backs up “{folder}”. Turn it on per computer, on its page.

@settingsPhotoFolderBacksUp.description: Caption showing the backed-up photo folder

@settingsDemo.description: Settings section label for the demo tools

settingsDemoCaption: Simulated devices until the Linksy core is connected. These start what another device would.

@settingsDemoReceivePairing.description: Demo action: simulate an incoming pairing request

@settingsDemoReceiveClipboard.description: Demo action: simulate incoming clipboard text

settingsTagline:
Your devices, connected.
No account, no cloud.

@settingsTagline.description: App tagline at the bottom of Settings (two lines)

settingsNameCaption: Your other devices see this name.

@settingsRename.description: Accessibility label of the phone card; name is the phone name

@settingsThisPhone.description: Under the phone name; shortId is a short device code

@settingsPermissionsRow.description: Settings row that opens the permissions sheet

settingsPermissionsWhat: What Linksy asks Android for, and why.

@settingsPermissionsWhat.description: Caption of the permissions row while loading

@settingsPermissionsBoth.description: Caption when both permissions are allowed

settingsPermissionsSome: {count, plural, other{{count} of 2 allowed. Tap to allow the rest.}}

@settingsPermissionsSome.description: Caption when some of the 2 permissions are allowed

permissionsIntro: Linksy asks only for what it needs, and you can change any of these later in Settings.

@permissionsIntro.description: Intro text of the permissions sheet

permissionsNotificationsWhy: Shows when a computer sees your screen or uses your camera, with a button to stop it.

@permissionsNotificationsWhy.description: Why the app needs the notifications permission

permissionsCameraWhy: Scans the pairing QR code, and lets a computer use this phone as a webcam when you allow it.

@permissionsCameraWhy.description: Why the app needs the camera permission

@permissionsAllow.description: Button that asks Android for a permission

@permissionsAllowed.description: Shown when a permission is already granted

@permissionsDone.description: Button that closes the permissions sheet

@remoteBack.description: Tooltip of the back button on the Remote screen

@remoteTitle.description: Title of the screen that uses the phone as a computer remote

@remoteAllowOn.description: Title while waiting for the computer to allow remote control; name is the computer

remoteAsks: Linksy on {name} asks whether this phone may move its pointer and type.

@remoteAsks.description: Detail while waiting for the computer to allow remote control

@remoteFailed.description: Title when the remote could not start

@remoteStopped.description: Title when the computer ended the remote

@remoteEndedBy.description: Detail when the computer ended the remote; name is the computer

@remoteTryAgain.description: Button that retries starting the remote

remoteTouchpadHint:
Move with one finger, tap to click
Two fingers scroll, two-finger tap right-clicks

@remoteTouchpadHint.description: Hint on the touchpad area (two lines)

@remoteKeyboard.description: Button that shows the keyboard to type on the computer

@remoteNextSlide.description: Accessibility label of the Next button

@remotePreviousSlide.description: Accessibility label of the Back button

@remoteStartShow.description: Button that starts the slideshow (sends F5)

@remoteEndShow.description: Button that ends the slideshow (sends Esc)

remoteVolumeHint: Volume down: next · Volume up: back. The screen stays on.

@ringTitle.description: Big title while the phone rings because a computer is looking for it

@ringLookingFor.description: Under the title; name is the computer that rings the phone
